name: Ramaskandam Hanumantam
text:
Ramaskandam Hanumantam,
Vainateyam Vrikodaram,
Shankaram Shankarasyesham,
Sarvanamami Sadanugam.
(Shayane Yah Smaren Nityam, Duswapnam Tasya Nashyati)
meaning: I bow to Rama, Skanda and Hanuman, to Vainateya (Garuda) and Vrikodara (Bhima), and to Shankara (Shiva): to all of them, always, I bow. (The bracketed line, often added: whoever remembers these names every night at bedtime is freed from bad dreams.)
note: Sarvakali chants the first four lines as the mantra. The bracketed half is the commonly recited ending; she leaves it out on purpose, so the mantra is not limited to warding off bad dreams.
source: Sarvakali’s teaching; the bracketed line is the common published ending
pronunciation: raa-ma-skan-dam ha-nu-man-tam; vai-na-tay-yam vri-ko-da-ram; shan-ka-ram shan-ka-ras-yay-sham; sar-va-na-maa-mi sa-daa-nu-gam; (sha-ya-nay yah sma-ren ni-tyam, du-swap-nam tas-ya naash-ya-ti)
